findings.title: 'Integrate now' silently threw away 8 of 9 subs and presented the 1-frame result as a finished master, with no error, warning or count anywhere in the UI
findings.what_happened: With 9 accepted 300s subs, clicking 'Integrate now' produced a master card reading 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' and no other feedback: no toast, no error banner, no 'x of y subs rejected' line. The database shows integrated_master_frames has 1 accepted row and 8 rows with rejection_reason 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=N, need >= 3', and integrated_masters.stats_json is {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,...}. Two distinct failures compound: (a) the integrator picked sub 1 as the alignment reference, detected 0 stars in it, and then failed every other sub against that empty reference instead of choosing a different reference or aborting; (b) the count of dropped subs exists in the outcome and in the DB but is never rendered for a manual integration.
findings.expected: Two things. (1) A reference frame with 0 detected stars must not be accepted as the reference -- fall back to the next-best frame (frames 4-9 each detected 29-30 stars) or abort with 'could not find a usable reference frame'. (2) Integration must report its own result: 'Integrated 1 of 9 subs - 8 failed to register' with the reason, exactly as the automatic-integration path already does (auto_integration_service.dart:378 builds precisely that sentence). Losing 89% of a night's data must never be silent.
findings.repro: 1. Seed 10 lights for one session with real FITS star fields (star sigma 1.0-2.25 px). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles. 3. Workbench > 'Reject HFR above' at 3.5 (leaves 9 accepted). 4. Scroll the right column to Integration settings, click 'Integrate now'. 5. Wait ~40 s. 6. Read the Masters card and look for any error surface.
findings.evidence: UI after the run: Masters card 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-24.png), header still '9 accepted - 1 rejected', no toast (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select image_id,accepted,rejection_reason from integrated_master_frames where master_id=2" -> 1|1|(null) then 8 rows 0|'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4..30, need >= 3'. stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8}. App log: '[STAR_DETECT] Detected 0 stars after filtering' on the reference frame.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() -- the returned outcome is stored in state.lastOutcome but workbench_view.dart:190 uses it only for a preview path and a button label; framesIntegrated/framesRejected are never rendered. Reference selection is in the native post-session integration path.
findings.proposed_fix: In integrate(), after the outcome returns, if outcome.result.framesRejected > 0 raise a warning toast + a persistent banner on the master card carrying the count and the most common rejection_reason; reuse auto_integration_service.dart's existing summary builder. Separately, make reference selection reject a candidate with fewer than the minimum registrable stars and retry with the next candidate before failing the run.

findings.title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
findings.what_happened: The improvement curve is derived from the master that was just produced. Because that master contained only 1 registered frame (see the P0 above), the persisted curve has one point and a recommendation of {keepN: 1, predictedSnrGainPct: 0.0, reason: 'Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)'}. The cull rail then renders an enabled primary action 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' whose tooltip is 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best 1 subs (+0% SNR)'. Pressing it three times changed nothing (still 9 accepted in the DB) and toasted 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. So the control knows the curve does not match the 9 accepted subs, yet still renders a specific, quantified, actionable label -- and its remedy is to re-run the same integration that produced the stale curve.
findings.expected: The rail must decide staleness at render time, not at press time. When the curve's population does not cover the currently-accepted subs, or when predictedSnrGainPct <= 0, show a disabled/absent action (or an explicit 'analysis out of date' chip) rather than a confident 'Keep best 1 (+0%)'. A control should not offer an operation it will unconditionally refuse.
findings.repro: 1. Do the Integrate-now repro above (produces a 1-frame master). 2. A new button 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' appears beside Blink mode / Select-lasso. 3. Click it. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db "select count(*) from captured_images where session_id=1 and is_accepted=1" -> still 9; toast reads 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png, rsr-22.png, rsr-25.png show 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' while the header reads '9 accepted - 1 rejected'; AT-SPI tree after the click contains 'panel: Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. DB improvement_curve_json for master 2: {"points":[{"n":1,...}],"recommendation":{"keepN":1,"keptIndices":[0],"predictedSnrGainPct":0.0,"reason":"Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)"},"population":[".../audit_L_001.fits"]} -- population length 1 vs 9 accepted, which is exactly the staleCurve guard in session_review_controller.dart:1377.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/widgets/sub_cull_rail.dart:473 (tooltip) and :475 (label 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct}%)'); guard in session_review_controller.dart:1354 cullToRecommended()
findings.proposed_fix: Lift the population-vs-accepted comparison out of cullToRecommended() into a getter the rail reads while building, and gate the button on it plus predictedSnrGainPct > 0.

findings.title: Project-growth panel groups subs by UTC calendar day, so one continuous evening is reported as two nights and every night is dated a day late
findings.what_happened: Session Review (narrative) 'This project over time' reports '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights' with x-axis labels Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, and 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h'. The database contains exactly THREE observing sessions (Audit Night A on the evening of Jul 25 local, B on Jul 27 local, C on Jul 29 local). Audit Night C is one continuous 50-minute run (19:30-20:20 America/New_York) that straddles 00:00 UTC, and the panel splits it into two separate 'nights' (Jul 29 with 4 frames, Jul 30 with 4 frames). Every other night is also labelled with the following calendar day because 21:00 EDT is 01:00 UTC.
findings.expected: Nights should be grouped by OBSERVING night in the site's local time (the conventional noon-to-noon boundary), so three sessions produce three points labelled Jul 25, Jul 27, Jul 29 and the panel says '3 nights'. Never a UTC calendar day: for any observer west of Greenwich the label is a day late, and for any observer east of Greenwich (all of Europe/Asia) the 00:00 UTC boundary falls in the MIDDLE of the observing night, splitting every single night in two.
findings.repro: 1. Seed three sessions of M51 lights, the third spanning 19:30-20:20 America/New_York on 2026-07-29 (crosses 00:00 UTC). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles (Review & Integrate). 3. Scroll the narrative view to 'This project over time'.
findings.evidence: UI: '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-08.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch') utc, strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch','localtime') local, count(*) from captured_images group by 1" -> 2026-07-26|2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-28|2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|2026-07-29|4. Three local nights, four UTC days.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_project_service.dart:679 _dayOf() -> DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); used by growthCurve(), bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice()
findings.proposed_fix: Group by observing night, not UTC date: shift the timestamp by the site's UTC offset and then by -12h before truncating to a day (the standard 'noon-to-noon' night key), and label the point with that local date. bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice() share _dayOf and are wrong in the same way -- a European user's 'best night' is currently the better HALF of a night.

findings.title: Narrowband mixer 'Apply palette' is a dead control: no composite, no file, no error, no log line
findings.what_happened: With three finalized single-filter masters for the target (Ha 20 frames, OIII 15, SII 10), the Narrowband mixer renders correctly, SHO/HOO presets populate the weight matrix correctly, and 'Apply palette' is enabled. Pressing it five times (three via click-img, twice via a raw xdotool click on the hovered button) produced nothing at all: narrowband_composites stayed at 0 rows, no FITS was written anywhere on disk, no toast appeared in the accessibility tree on six consecutive polls, and the app log recorded no combine activity. The screen's toast path is demonstrably alive -- the same session surfaced 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling' from the cull rail -- and the neighbouring 'Run both' A/B button responded immediately with a 'Preview...' state and native STAR_DETECT log lines, so neither the toast machinery nor the click mapping explains the silence.
findings.expected: Apply palette should either produce a narrowband_composites row plus an on-disk composite FITS and render it in the composite card, or fail loudly with the reason ('Need at least two finalized narrowband masters to combine.' is already written for that case). Silently doing nothing on the mixer's only action makes the whole SHO/HOO feature untestable by the user.
findings.repro: 1. Seed three finalized integrated_masters for the target with filter Ha / OIII / SII and real master_fits_path files. 2. Session Review > Workbench > Refresh. 3. Scroll to 'Narrowband mixer', press SHO (matrix fills SII->R, Ha->G, OIII->B correctly). 4. Press 'Apply palette'. 5. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from narrowband_composites' -> 0; no new .fits under the masters output dir; no toast.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-30.png (mixer with 3 channels), rsr-33.png (SHO matrix + enabled Apply palette), rsr-35.png (cursor hovering the button, confirming the hit target). AT-SPI polls immediately after the click contain only 'panel: Combine matrix' -- no error node. DB: narrowband_composites count 0 after 5 presses. Log tail contains nothing between the click and the next discovery sweep.
findings.proposed_fix: Instrument runNarrowband with an entry log and surface every exit path (including the <2-input guard) through the same toast the cull rail uses; then fix whichever leg is swallowing the call. The button should also show a busy state while combiningNarrowband is true, which would have made the no-op visible.

findings.title: Narrowband mixer opens with every channel weight at 0.00, i.e. a palette that renders black
findings.what_happened: With Ha, OIII and SII masters present the mixer opens labelled 'Custom mix' with all nine R/G/B weights at 0.00. Applying that state would map every channel to zero.
findings.expected: When the resolved channel set is Ha+OIII+SII, default to SHO; when it is Ha+OIII only, default to HOO; when it is a single narrowband master, default that channel to a luminance mapping. A user should never have to make three clicks to get out of a state that cannot produce an image.
findings.repro: 1. Seed Ha/OIII/SII masters. 2. Session Review > Workbench > Narrowband mixer. 3. Read the nine weight values and the 'Custom mix' label.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-30.png: 'Narrowband palette ... Custom mix', SII R 0.00 G 0.00 B 0.00, OIII R 0.00 G 0.00 B 0.00, Ha (below fold) likewise; AT-SPI tree before pressing SHO showed all 0.00.
findings.proposed_fix: Initialise _palette/_weights from the best-matching preset for widget.channels in initState/didUpdateWidget instead of 'custom' + zeros.

findings.title: sub_gallery_panel.dart (601 lines) is built by no screen -- only by a widget test -- while the code claims the narrative view uses it
findings.what_happened: Grepping every .dart file under packages/ and apps/ finds exactly one construction of SubGalleryPanel, in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_dynamic_subs_test.dart:102. Neither narrative_view.dart nor workbench_view.dart references it, and driving the app confirms it: the narrative view renders hero preview, Night Doctor, improvement curve, findings, project growth and the calibration cards, and contains no sub grid at all. sub_cull_rail.dart:24 states 'One controller, two renderings: the narrative screen uses SubGalleryPanel', which is not true of the shipped build.
findings.expected: Either the narrative view shows the sub gallery (as the comment says and as the two-renderings design implies), or the dead panel and its comment are deleted. As shipped, a user reviewing a night in Narrative mode has no way to see, blink, accept or reject individual subs without switching to Workbench.
findings.repro: 1. Open Session Review for any session. 2. Stay in Narrative and scroll top to bottom -- no sub grid appears. 3. grep -rn 'SubGalleryPanel(' packages apps --include='*.dart' -> one hit, in a test.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-07.png, rsr-09.png, rsr-10.png cover the entire narrative scroll: sections are 'How deep is deep enough?', 'What I fixed and found', 'This project over time', 'Calibrated & annotated'. grep output as above.
findings.proposed_fix: Mount SubGalleryPanel in narrative_view.dart under a 'Your subs' section, or delete the file and correct the sub_cull_rail doc comment.

findings.title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
findings.what_happened: Selecting each of the five integration profiles in turn and diffing the whole ADVANCED block of the accessibility tree: Fast changes the resampler to Bilinear, Few Subs changes rejection to Percentile clip with 0.2/0.1, Long Night / Gradient changes normalization Mode from Global to Local grid -- but Balanced and Maximum Quality produce an IDENTICAL 30-line block (`diff bal.txt maxq.txt` is empty) and an identical summary sentence. The source confirms it: IntegrationSettings.preset(maximumQuality) sets resampler=lanczos3, weighting=snrSquared, generateRejectionMap=true, cosmeticCorrection=true, outputBitDepth=f32 -- every one of which is already the constructor default that balanced inherits. The only field that differs between the two presets is sourcePreset, which is a label.
findings.expected: A profile named 'Maximum Quality' must actually cost something in exchange for quality -- e.g. a tighter RANSAC threshold, more reference stars, local normalization, linear-fit/percentile rejection tuned for the sub count, or drizzle. As shipped, a user who deliberately picks Maximum Quality over Balanced for their best data gets exactly the same stack and is misled about it.
findings.repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > Integration settings > expand Advanced settings. 2. Click 'Balanced', capture the ALIGNMENT..DRIZZLE block of `drive_linux.py tree`. 3. Click 'Maximum Quality', capture again. 4. diff -> no differences. 5. Repeat for 'Long Night / Gradient' -> exactly one line differs (Global -> Local grid), proving the capture method detects real changes.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/maxq.txt -> identical (30 lines each); /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/ln.txt -> 1 line differs. Summary line unchanged: 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma. Recommends culling the worst 10%.' for both. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:737-745 vs the constructor defaults at :672,:676,:690,:691,:692.
findings.proposed_fix: Give maximumQuality settings that actually differ (e.g. ransacThresholdPx 1.5, maxRefStars 120, normalization local, reject linearFit) -- or drop the chip. Also make the panel's one-line summary mention the knobs the chosen profile changed, so three profiles cannot render the same sentence.

findings.title: Running an A/B recipe preview leaves a full 'Preview... 100%' progress bar pinned under the header forever, so the screen permanently claims a job is running
findings.what_happened: Pressing 'Run both' in the A/B recipe compare panel puts a green progress strip labelled 'Preview... 100%' between the Narrative/Workbench toggle and the content. The two previews completed (the panel filled in with 'Frames kept tie 1 vs 1', 'Residual tie 0.00 vs 0.00 px', 'Integration time tie 00:05:00 vs 00:05:00'), but the strip was still on screen 13 minutes later, survived switching to Narrative and back, and is still present in the AT-SPI tree as 'panel: Preview...'.
findings.expected: The strip must clear when the action that raised it finishes. The controller's own comment says a terminal 1.0 fraction 'is left on screen until the action's own completion handler clears it' -- integrate() does clear it (clearProgress/clearLiveProgress) but reIntegratePreview(), which is what the A/B panel calls, has no such handler, so the strip is orphaned.
findings.repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > A / B compare > 'Run both'. 2. Wait for both preview cards to fill in. 3. The strip under the header still reads 'Preview... 100%'. 4. Toggle to Narrative and back -- still there. 5. `drive_linux.py tree | grep Preview` still returns 'panel: Preview...'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-36.png (strip at 100% with the A/B results already rendered above it), rsr-37.png / rsr-38.png (same strip 13 min later, in Narrative and in Workbench). AT-SPI: 'panel: Preview...' persists across polls.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:515 _bindProgress() and :976 reIntegratePreview() (no clearProgress on completion); rendered by session_review_screen.dart:119 _ProgressStrip
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap reIntegratePreview (and the other seam-driven actions: runColorCalibration, runBackgroundExtraction, runDeconvolve, runStarReduction, runNarrowband) in the same try/finally that clears progress on exit, or clear progress centrally whenever `busy` transitions back to false.

findings.title: A/B recipe compare declared 'tie 1 vs 1' when both recipes had silently dropped 8 of 9 subs
findings.what_happened: After the failed 9-sub integration, 'Run both' in A/B compare produced 'Frames kept  tie  1 vs 1', 'Residual  tie  0.00 vs 0.00 px', 'Integration time  tie  00:05:00 vs 00:05:00'. Both recipes registered only 1 of the 9 accepted subs, and the panel presents that as a neutral tie between two recipes rather than as two failed runs. A user comparing recipes would conclude the two are equivalent, when in fact neither produced a usable stack.
findings.expected: When framesKept is far below the accepted-sub count the comparison is meaningless and must say so -- e.g. 'Recipe A registered 1 of 9 subs; recipe B registered 1 of 9. Neither result is comparable.' A 'tie' verdict on two degenerate stacks is a false statement about the data.
findings.repro: 1. With 9 accepted subs whose reference frame yields no detectable stars, Session Review > Workbench > A / B compare > 'Run both'. 2. Read the verdict row.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-36.png: 'Frames kept tie 1 vs 1 | Residual tie 0.00 vs 0.00 px | Integration time tie 00:05:00 vs 00:05:00', while the header reads '9 accepted - 1 rejected'.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare framesIntegrated against the accepted-sub count and render a warning verdict when either side registered fewer than, say, 80% of the subs, instead of a tie/winner chip.
